$comment: Schema for a single persona object. Used in .code-beta/personas.json (array of these) or generated at runtime.

id.$comment: Hyphenated slug. Unique within a run. Used in report filenames and rubric tables.

description.$comment: 2-3 sentences: who this person is, what they want, what state they're in.
description.example: A user who signed up two weeks ago and is returning to the app after their session token expired. They're on an iPhone using Safari. They want to resume where they left off without having to remember their password.

entryPoint.$comment: The specific code surface or UI flow where this persona enters the changed feature.
entryPoint.example: POST /api/auth/refresh — called automatically by the client when a 401 is received

goal.$comment: One sentence: what outcome the persona is trying to achieve.
goal.example: Resume their session transparently without being redirected to the login page

constraints.$comment: Array of constraints that distinguish this persona from others: device, permission level, data state, etc.
example: iOS Safari — virtual keyboard overlaps lower UI elements
Expired access token but valid refresh token in httpOnly cookie

inferredFrom.$comment: Explains which codebase signals led to this persona being inferred. Omit in hand-authored .code-beta/personas.json.
inferredFrom.example: session.ts line 47 checks refresh token validity; middleware/auth.ts has iOS Safari UA detection

example.name: Returning Mobile User
example.description: A user who signed up two weeks ago and is returning after their session expired. On iPhone Safari. Wants to resume without re-entering their password.
example.entryPoint: POST /api/auth/refresh — triggered automatically by the SWR client on 401
example.goal: Resume session transparently without hitting the login page
constraints: iOS Safari — virtual keyboard overlaps lower UI elements
Has a valid refresh token in httpOnly cookie
example.inferredFrom: session.ts:47 refresh logic, middleware/auth.ts iOS Safari UA check
